slides.texte_overlay:
habits that make you
fearless around anyone

saying it plainly

say what you mean in one simple sentence instead of hiding it in a long apology. plain words sound calm and certain, and people take them far more seriously.

asking one more question

when someone says something unclear, ask what they meant. a calm, simple question takes away their power to make you feel small, flustered or confused.

practising small discomfort

do one slightly uncomfortable thing a day, like a phone call or a question in class. each small one makes the next big moment feel far less scary and much easier.

understanding people

learning how people think makes them far less scary. 5 minutes a day on one idea from psychology, like why we people please, goes a surprisingly long way.

slides.texte_overlay:
no long excuses

when you say no, keep it short and kind. long explanations sound like you're asking for permission, while a short answer sounds calm and sure of itself.
